newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel asks Palestinians to help in stabbing case.
newsitem.headline: Israel asks Palestinians to help in stabbing case.

text.p: Israeli police on Saturday asked Palestinian police to help investigate the stabbing deaths of two Israeli women found in the West Bank on Friday, a police spokeswoman said.
"The Israeli police have asked the help of Palestinian police, to provide any clue," the spokeswoman said.
The stabbed bodies were found by hikers in the Wadi Qelt nature reserve in the West Bank, about five km (three miles) from the Palestinian-ruled Jericho enclave.
Israeli police said they were investigating the possibility the murders were politically motivated by Palestinians.
The spokeswoman said autopsies on the two bodies ruled out suspicions they were raped, strengthening the possibility of a "nationalist" motive.

The women were identified as Hagit Zavitsky of the Jewish settlement Kfar Adumim in the West Bank between Jerusalem and Jericho, and Liat Kastiel of the town of Holon near Tel Aviv. Both were 23 years old.
A friend of Kastiel told Israel Radio the women worked together as security guards at one of Israel's border crossings to Jordan.
The chief of Israeli police in the West Bank told Army Radio police and army forces were searching the Wadi Qelt area for footprints, evidence or witnesses.
"We are talking about an area where in the past there were attacks by Palestinian guerrillas," said police commander Yossi Sidbon.
Asked what indication there was that Palestinians could have committed the murders, Sidbon said:
"The stabbing, the place of the murder which is not a place for hikes and is not near criminal elements. We are checking a nationalist motive but do not rule out criminal activity."
Police had said on Friday that the victims were teenagers.
In July 1995, two Israelis were found in the Wadi Qelt area shot and stabbed to death in an unsolved case. In October 1993, Palestinian guerrillas killed two Israeli hikers in Wadi Qelt.
